colophon: Thus ends the Sri Rama Raksha Stotra, composed by Sri Budhakaushika.

lines.1: Of this mantra, the Sri Rama Raksha Stotra: the seer is Budhakaushika;
lines.2: the deity is Sita and Ramachandra; the meter is anushtubh;
lines.3: Sita is its power; the glorious Hanuman is its pin, the lock that holds it fast;
lines.4: its use: recitation of the Rama Raksha Stotra, for the pleasure of Sri Ramachandra.
lines.5: Let one meditate on him: arms reaching to the knees, holding bow and arrow, seated in the bound lotus posture,
lines.6: wearing yellow cloth, eyes rivaling fresh lotus petals, serene;
lines.7: his eyes meeting the lotus face of Sita, seated on his left lap; dark as a rain cloud;
lines.8: shining with many ornaments, crowned with a great mass of matted hair: Ramachandra.
lines.9: The story of the lord of the Raghus spreads across a thousand million verses;
lines.10: every single syllable of it destroys even the gravest sins of those who hear it.
lines.11: Meditating on Rama, dark as the blue lotus, lotus-eyed,
lines.12: with Janaki and Lakshmana beside him, crowned with matted locks,
lines.13: sword, quiver, bow and arrow in hand, ender of the night-prowling demons,
lines.14: the unborn, all-pervading one, who appeared in play to protect the world,
lines.15: let the wise recite this Rama-shield, slayer of sin, granter of every wish:
lines.16: may Raghava protect my head; the son of Dasharatha, my forehead.
lines.17: May Kausalya's son protect my eyes; Vishvamitra's beloved, my ears;
lines.18: may the guardian of the sacrifice protect my nose; he who loves Lakshmana, my mouth.
lines.19: May the treasury of knowledge protect my tongue; he whom Bharata reveres, my throat;
lines.20: may the bearer of divine weapons protect my shoulders; the breaker of Shiva's bow, my arms.
lines.21: May Sita's lord protect my hands; the victor over Parashurama, my heart;
lines.22: may the destroyer of Khara protect my waist; the refuge of Jambavan, my navel.
lines.23: May Sugriva's lord protect my hips; Hanuman's master, my haunches;
lines.24: may the best of the Raghus, destroyer of the demon clans, protect my thighs.
lines.25: May the builder of the bridge protect my knees; the slayer of ten-headed Ravana, my shins;
lines.26: may he who gave Vibhishana his fortune protect my feet; may Rama protect my whole body.
lines.27: The virtuous one who recites this shield, charged with Rama's strength,
lines.28: will be long-lived, happy, blessed with children, victorious, and humble.
lines.29: Those who roam the underworld, the earth, and the sky, and those who move in disguise,
lines.30: cannot so much as look upon one who is guarded by the names of Rama.
lines.32: a person is not stained by sins, and gains both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
lines.33: This one world-conquering mantra, guarded by the name of Rama:
lines.34: whoever wears it at the throat holds every attainment in the palm of their hand.
lines.35: Whoever remembers this armor of Rama, called the Diamond Cage,
lines.36: has a command that goes unchallenged everywhere, and wins victory and blessing.
lines.37: Just as Shiva taught this Rama-shield in a dream,
lines.38: so Budhakaushika, waking at dawn, wrote it down.
lines.39: A garden of wish-fulfilling trees, the end of every calamity,
lines.40: the delight of the three worlds: glorious Rama is our lord.
lines.42: wide-eyed as white lotuses, dressed in bark cloth and black deerskin,
lines.43: living on fruit and roots, self-controlled, ascetics, celibate:
lines.44: these two sons of Dasharatha, the brothers Rama and Lakshmana,
lines.45: refuge of all beings, best of all archers,
lines.46: destroyers of the demon clans: may these two best of the Raghus protect us.
lines.47: Bows strung and ready, hands on their arrows, carrying quivers of swift, inexhaustible shafts:
lines.48: may Rama and Lakshmana always walk ahead of me on the road, to protect me.
lines.49: Armed and armored, sword at his side, bearing bow and arrows, youthful,
lines.50: going before us as our heart's desire: may Rama, with Lakshmana, protect us.
lines.51: Rama, son of Dasharatha, the hero, followed by Lakshmana, the strong one,
lines.52: descendant of Kakutstha, the complete Person, Kausalya's son, best of the Raghus,
lines.53: known through the Vedanta, lord of sacrifice, the ancient supreme Person,
lines.54: beloved of Janaki, glorious, of immeasurable valor:
lines.55: my devotee who, full of faith, chants these names every day
lines.56: gains merit greater than the horse sacrifice; there is no doubt.
lines.57: Those who praise Rama, dark as a blade of durva grass, lotus-eyed, clad in yellow,
lines.58: with his divine names are no longer bound to the round of rebirth.
lines.59: Rama, Lakshmana's elder brother, best of the Raghus, Sita's lord, the beautiful one,
lines.60: descendant of Kakutstha, ocean of compassion, treasury of virtues, dear to the learned, righteous,
lines.61: king of kings, true to his word, son of Dasharatha, dark-hued, peace embodied:
lines.62: I bow to Raghava, the delight of the world, jewel of the Raghu line, the enemy of Ravana.
lines.63: To Rama, to Ramabhadra, to Ramachandra, the creator,
lines.64: to the chief of the Raghus, the protector, to Sita's lord: salutation.
lines.65: Sri Rama, Rama, joy of the Raghus, Rama, Rama;
lines.66: Sri Rama, Rama, elder brother of Bharata, Rama, Rama;
lines.67: Sri Rama, Rama, fierce in battle, Rama, Rama;
lines.68: Sri Rama, Rama, be my refuge, Rama, Rama.
lines.69: The feet of Sri Ramachandra I remember with my mind;
lines.70: the feet of Sri Ramachandra I praise with my speech;
lines.71: to the feet of Sri Ramachandra I bow with my head;
lines.72: in the feet of Sri Ramachandra I take refuge.
lines.73: Rama is my mother; Ramachandra, my father;
lines.74: Rama is my master; Ramachandra, my friend;
lines.76: no other do I know, none at all, none.
lines.77: He who has Lakshmana at his right and Janaka's daughter at his left,
lines.78: and Maruti before him: to him, the joy of the Raghus, I bow.
lines.79: The delight of the world, steadfast on the stage of battle,
lines.80: lotus-eyed, lord of the Raghu dynasty,
lines.81: compassion in form, the source of mercy:
lines.82: in Sri Ramachandra I take refuge.
lines.83: Swift as the mind, fast as the wind,
lines.84: master of the senses, foremost of the wise,
lines.85: son of the wind, chief of the monkey hosts:
lines.86: in Rama's messenger I take refuge.
lines.87: Singing 'Rama, Rama,' sweetly, in sweet syllables,
lines.88: perched on the branch of poetry: I bow to Valmiki, the cuckoo.
lines.89: Remover of calamities, giver of every prosperity,
lines.90: delight of the world: to Sri Rama I bow again and again.
lines.91: It roasts the seeds of rebirth, earns the riches of happiness,
lines.92: and terrifies the messengers of Death: this roar of 'Rama, Rama.'
lines.93: Rama, jewel of kings, is ever victorious; I worship Rama, the lord of Lakshmi;
lines.94: by Rama the armies of the night-prowlers were struck down; to that Rama, salutation;
lines.95: there is no refuge higher than Rama; I am the servant of Rama;
lines.96: may my mind always dissolve in Rama; O Rama, lift me up.
lines.97: 'Sri Rama, Rama, Rama': thus I delight in Rama, O lovely one;
lines.98: the name of Rama, O fair-faced one, is equal to the thousand names.
